title: introduce-session-consistency-smoke-orchestrator-and-persona-preservation-metrics
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Added a smoke orchestration harness for multi-turn session consistency checks and a persona-preservation metric for paraphrase robustness. No API changes. Opt-in by default via smoke pipeline flag.
description:
Context: We see intermittent production regressions where multi-turn behavior drifts after model updates even when single-turn metrics look stable. This PR adds an end-to-end smoke orchestrator that replays short synthetic user journeys to catch regressions in turn-level coherence, stability of slot values across turns, and latency regressions under burst load. It also introduces a persona-preservation metric that measures whether paraphrase-based rephrasings of user turns preserve persona-specific tokens and slot assignments.

Goals: 1) Provide a lightweight, fast-running CI smoke job that executes representative 3-6 turn sessions with controlled paraphrase/noise variants. 2) Surface per-turn regression deltas and a single-line pass/fail decision to gate merges for runtime branches. 3) Emit telemetry and provenance so results are reproducible and debuggable.

What I changed:
- New harness: eval-harness/smoke/session_orchestrator.py implements session templates, replay engine, synthetic user mutation strategies (paraphrase, punctuation/noise, entity-order swaps) and a TTL-based concurrency runner that keeps runs under 3 minutes per matrix cell.
- New metrics: eval-harness/metrics/persona_preservation.py computes token overlap weighted by slot importance, plus a contextual-stability score that penalizes contradictory slot values.
- Config: eval-harness/config/smoke_profiles.yaml contains short session presets used by the orchestrator and a small default workload for CI.
- CI pipeline: .github/workflows/smoke-eval.yml runs the orchestrator in a matrix across release/main and a representative small model set; includes a toggle to run in amazon-ci vs local docker.
- Tests: tests/smoke/test_session_consistency.py contains deterministic unit tests for the mutation operators and an integration smoke test that runs a tiny mocked runtime to validate reporting shapes.
- Docs: docs/eval-smoke.md explains how to author session presets and how to interpret persona-preservation outputs.
- Examples: examples/smoke-presets/ contains three short session presets (support_flow.json, checkout_flow.json, assistant_onboarding.json).

Backwards compatibility: This is opt-in for project-level CI; nothing changes default eval harness behavior. The orchestrator is modular and can be wired into more exhaustive evals later.

Checklist: [x] unit tests for mutation operators [x] integration smoke test with mocked runtime [x] CI pipeline added and green [x] docs and examples added [x] telemetry & result export in CSV/JSON

PR size rationale: larger because we add a small new subsystem and example presets; files are intentionally small and focused.

How to run locally: python -m eval_harness.smoke.session_orchestrator --profile examples/smoke-presets/support_flow.json --out ./tmp/report.json

Notes on metrics and thresholds: persona-preservation produces a normalized score 0..1; CI profile uses a default threshold of 0.72 for pass. The orchestrator also asserts per-turn latency median <= 350ms for the small-model matrix; latency SLO is configurable in smoke_profiles.yaml.

Signal integration: CI publishes a concise JSON summary that includes per-session diffs, failure categories (paraphrase-flip, slot-inversion, latency-outlier) and suggested investigation steps.

Related work: motivated by ENG-2114 (session regression post-model-update) and ENG-2198 (paraphrase robustness task).
